title.narrative: Provision of Integrated Life-saving Nutrition, Health, WASH Support to Conflict- Affected Populations in Bama, Konduga, and Magumeri LGAs, Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed intervention seeks to address the urgent WASH, Nutrition and Health needs of vulnerable populations in Bama, Magumeri, and Konduga LGAs of Borno State, in alignment with the 2025 Lean Season Multi-Sectoral Plan and the NHF Standard Allocation strategy. The project targets communities facing crisis or emergency levels of food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 and 4), compounded by inadequate access to essential WASH and nutrition services, high rates of acute malnutrition, and increased vulnerability to disease outbreaks during the rainy season. The project will reach 4,600 in Bama for WASH activities, 2500 for Health in Konduga and 2500 in Magumeri for Nutrition activities.ltbrgtIn Magumeri, where communities are severely impacted by ongoing protracted conflict and food insecurity, the project will deliver integrated Nutrition services. Nutrition interventions will include active case finding for acute malnutrition, treatment of severe and moderate acute malnutrition (SAM/MAM) among children under five and pregnant and breastfeeding women (PBWG), MIYCN counselling, and community sensitization on appropriate infant and young child feeding practices. These services will be complemented by WASH interventions to reduce exposure to waterborne diseases and improve treatment outcomes. WASH activities will include provision of safe water through water trucking and rehabilitation of water systems, hygiene promotion, and installation of gender-segregated emergency latrines and handwashing stations.ltbrgtIn Bama LGA, where WASH conditions remain critical and the risk of waterborne disease outbreaks is high due to overcrowded IDP camps and poor sanitation, the project will focus solely on lifesaving WASH interventions. Activities will prioritize the provision of chlorinated water, desludging of latrines in high-risk locations, and hygiene awareness campaigns targeting women, girls, and other vulnerable groups. ltspangtIn Konduga, SHlt/spangtltspangtO willt/spangtltspangtl implement a Healthlt/spangtltspangt response.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtNutrition sites will be linked with health facilities for managing complicated SAM through referral. ltspangtThe project will incorporate Protection Mainstreaming, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), and Gender Equality and Disability Inclusion principles across all interventions. Community engagement and feedback mechanisms will be deployed to ensure that interventions are tailored, accessible, and responsive to the needs of women, children, persons with disablt/spangtltspangtilities, and other at-risk groups.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtThrough this integrated, area-based approach, the project aims to contribute to the reduction of acute malnutrition, prevent WASH-related disease outbreaks, contribute to the wellbeing of the community members and strengthen community resilience during the lean season. The intervention aligns with the NHF 2025 strategic objectives to mitigate food insecurity, malnutrition and associated protection risks while reinforcing local capacity and preparedness for seasonal and conflict-induced emergencies.lt/pgt
